title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 339
paragraphs: Down to the time when Rhampsinitos was king, they told me, there was nothing in Egypt but orderly rule, and Egypt prospered greatly. But after him Cheops became king and brought them to every kind of misery. He shut up all the temples, and having first stopped them from sacrificing there, he then ordered all the Egyptians to work for him. Some were assigned to drag stones from the quarries in the Arabian mountains to the Nile; others he ordered to receive the stones after they had been ferried across the river in boats, and to haul them to the so-called Libyan mountains. They worked in shifts of a hundred thousand men at a time, for three months straight. Ten years of this oppression passed while the causeway was built along which they hauled the stones — a causeway that is, in my view, a work not much less than the pyramid itself. Its length is five furlongs, its breadth ten fathoms, and its height, where it is highest, eight fathoms, and it is made of smoothed stone with figures carved upon it. For this, they said, the ten years were spent, as well as for the underground chambers on the hill on which the pyramids stand, which he had made as burial chambers for himself on an island, having led a channel from the Nile to the place. For the construction of the pyramid itself a period of twenty years passed. The pyramid is square, each side measuring eight hundred feet, and its height is the same. It is built of smoothed stones fitted together in the most perfect manner, not one of the stones being less than thirty feet in length.
